column1: # SEEDS AND WHY: 002778C0 is the REGISTERED HANDLER - passed in r8 at 00276DE6 beside `mov edx, 0x2DC0` and `call 00245000` with storage `lea rcx, [rdi+0x220]` - so its rcx is this object BY CONSTRUCTION, which is this kit's own admissibility rule for widget arg0. The other eight are the functions that handler passes the object to in rcx, the same one-level rule scan_widget_one_level uses; 00244960 is already a CORE function in gen_widget_census, which is independent corroboration that the object is a widget. CORRECTED 2026-09-20 (OPUS) - ONE OF THE NINE SEEDS IS NOT WHAT THIS LINE SAYS IT IS: 00249C60 does NOT receive the object in rcx at any call site. Flow analysis of 002778C0 finds 13 calls to it, not the 3 recorded when this census was requested, and every one loads rcx with a SMALL INTEGER (`mov ecx, 5`, `mov ecx, 2`, `mov ecx, 0xa`, `mov ecx, edi`, `mov ecx, r12d`, `lea ecx, [r14 + 3]`). It takes an int. NO ROW IS AFFECTED - the emitter attributed nothing to it, which is exactly why a wrong seed could sit in this header unchallenged. The other eight are confirmed: an independent flow-sensitive scan recovers 002778C0, 00275440, 002753F0, 0027B430, 00244960, 002470D0, 002470C0 and 005C5230 with rcx proven to be this object. SECOND CORRECTION, TO THE ROWS: this emitter treats rsi as the object for the whole body after `mov rsi, rcx` at 002778FC. It is not. rsi is RELOADED from a stack slot at 00278701 and RE-BASED at 00278FD2 (`add rsi, 0x1600`) and 00278FE3 (`lea rsi, [rsi + 0x1620]`) inside a two-iteration loop. Six rows below are therefore marked `NOT-RECEIVER-PROVEN` and their displacements - 0x18A, 0x18E, 0x1600, 0x17A8 and 0x2C20 - are NOT fields of this type; all five lie inside the two declared children, and two of the six sites are `lea` instructions that touch no memory at all. The flow-sensitive census reports 30 receiver displacements against this file's 35, and adds 13 receiver-as-INDEX sites this emitter cannot see. See battle-menu-child-widget-1620-accesses.tsv and gfz-scripts/receiver_flow_census.py
